can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with a range of determiners before a superlative adjective. ► noun phrases

ontology.pedagogical_hook: determiner + superlative + noun — slot any determiner before the rank
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker frames the top rank against any context

positives: He is my best friend in the world.
That was their most important decision.
negatives: He is the best friend you can have.
They like most important things in life.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of focusing adverbs ('particularly', 'especially') to point to or highlight something. ► adverbs: position

ontology.pedagogical_hook: particularly / especially — spotlight one element from a presumed set
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker isolates one referent above others

positives: I like all animals, especially dogs.
The weather is particularly bad today.
negatives: He is a very special person.
She is particular about her food choices.

can_do_statement: Can use an adjective or adjective phrase after pronouns like 'something', 'nothing', 'somewhere', 'nowhere'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: something / nothing + adjective — leave the referent vague and color it
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker keeps the referent indeterminate while coloring it

positives: I want to show you something really interesting.
He gave me nothing useful today.
negatives: I saw something like a ghost in the dark.
He knew someone who was very rich.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs ('completely', 'obviously', 'clearly', 'actually', 'luckily', 'honestly', 'sadly', 'basically', 'obviously', 'hopefully') to indicate an attitude or viewpoint.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: completely / obviously / clearly / actually / luckily / honestly — dial the speaker's stance up or down
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker takes explicit ownership of the stance

positives: But actually, he did not come to the party.
Hopefully, it will not rain tomorrow.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of degree adverbs ('a little', 'a bit') with verbs to indicate degree or intensity. ► determiners

ontology.pedagogical_hook: a little / a bit — small step up from zero on the verb’s intensity dial
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker softens the verb’s force without abandoning it

negatives: I have a little money in my wallet.

guideword: FORM: 'THE BEST' WITH NOUN AND  'TO-' INFINITIVE
can_do_statement: Can use 'the best' before a noun + 'to'-infinitive.  ► clauses: comparative

ontology.pedagogical_hook: the best + noun + to + verb — name the top context for an action
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker positions an action as the top-of-its-kind purpose

positives: It is the best book to read.
This is the best computer to buy.
negatives: He is the best to play the game.
She sent the best procedure to the operation.

sub_category: adverbs and adverb phrases: types and meanings
can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of adverbs to indicate degrees of certainty.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: probably / possibly / certainly / definitely / surely / presumably — calibrate certainty at finer resolution
ontology.agency_or_distance: speaker calibrates commitment to the proposition

positives: I will probably go to the beach.
He is definitely coming to the party.
negatives: Maybe I will go to the store.

can_do_statement: Can use adjectives with the prefix a- ('asleep', 'awake', 'alive', 'alone') predicatively only, after linking verbs.

ontology.mental_model: a- adjectives are states, never glued before nouns
ontology.pedagogical_hook: a- words stay after the verb

positives: I feel completely alone right now.
negatives: He is afraid of the large spiders.
The awake baby cried all night long.

can_do_statement: Can use an imperative clause with 'let me' + base form of a main verb, as a focusing device, to introduce something

positives: Okay, let me check the schedule.
So, let me explain it to you.
